about.title: Banning Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: When a Banning family loses someone in a crash, the grief is heavy enough without also facing insurance calls, funeral bills, and confusing legal deadlines. Banning saw 104 injury collisions and 3 traffic deaths in the most recent reporting year, with many incidents clustering along I-10 and W Ramsey Street, especially on Friday evenings. California law gives surviving spouses, domestic partners, and children the first right to bring a wrongful death claim, with certain other dependents eligible if none of those survivors exist. These claims can include funeral and burial costs, lost financial support the person would have provided, and compensation for the loss of their love, companionship, and guidance. We handle wrongful death claims on a contingency basis, meaning no fee unless there's a recovery. Our team will explain your options, handle insurance communication, and work to pursue the claim on your family's behalf.

items.title: Standing Rules, Explained Clearly
items.desc: California limits who can file a wrongful death claim, starting with spouses, domestic partners, and children. We can help you understand where your family fits and what evidence supports your standing.

items.title: A Strict Two-Year Window
items.desc: California generally requires wrongful death claims to be filed within two years of the date of death, and that window shrinks significantly if a government entity is involved. Reaching out early helps protect your family's ability to pursue the case at all.

items.title: No Upfront Cost During a Difficult Time
items.desc: We work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless we recover compensation for your family. That structure lets you focus on grieving and healing instead of legal bills.

items.question: Who in my family is allowed to file a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: California law prioritizes the surviving spouse or domestic partner and children first. If none of those survivors exist, certain other dependents or heirs may have standing. We can review your family's specific situation and confirm who qualifies.

items.question: Is a wrongful death claim the same as a criminal case against the driver?
items.answer: No, they're entirely separate. A criminal case is brought by the state and focuses on punishment, while a wrongful death claim is a civil case a family files to recover financial losses and other damages. You can pursue a wrongful death claim regardless of whether criminal charges are filed.

items.question: Why does it matter that so many Banning crashes happen along I-10 and on Fridays?
items.answer: Public crash records show Banning's injury collisions often cluster on I-10 and W Ramsey Street, with a noticeable rise on Friday evenings between 6 and 8 p.m. That pattern can be relevant to gathering evidence, since traffic camera footage, witness availability, and highway patrol reports tend to be tied to those specific times and locations. We can use this context when investigating what happened.

items.question: What costs can my family recover in a wrongful death claim?
items.answer: Recoverable losses typically include funeral and burial expenses, the financial support your loved one would have provided, and compensation for the loss of their love, companionship, and guidance. Every family's losses look different, so we can walk through what applies to your circumstances.
